overview.body:
**Omphalós** ​(*omphalos*) — ‌Navel, ‌Center, Delphi ​· ​Navel (of ​the ​earth); the ​stone ‌at Delphi ​regarded ​as the ‌centre ​of the ‌world ​— belongs ‌to ​the Greek ​tradition, ​where it ​is ​catalogued under ‌the domain ​"Navel, ‌Center, Delphi". ​The ‌name means ​"Navel ‌(of the ​earth); ‌the stone ​at ​Delphi regarded ‌as ‌the centre ‌of ​the world"[^1].

​**Omphalós** ‌belongs to ​the ​Greek tradition, ‌where ​it is ​associated ‌with navel, ​center, ‌delphi.[^2]

PuniCodex ​restores ​the name ​as ​**Omphalós** and ‌serves ‌its temple ​at ‌[omphalós.com](https://xn--omphals-q0a.com). The ​original ​preserves one ‌prosodic ‌feature — ‌stress ‌or vowel ​length ‌— rather ​than ​both, which ​places ‌the name ​in Tier ​2. ​The plain ‌ASCII ​form *omphalos* ​survives ​as a ‌modern ​convenience imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ‌not the ​fallback, ​is the ​form ​the project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^3].

the-name.body:
The name ​is attested ‌in Greek ‌as **ὀμφαλός**. ​Etymologically it ​means "Navel ​(of the ​earth); the ​stone at ‌Delphi regarded ​as the ​centre of the ‌world"[^1].

The ​reconstructed proto-form ‌is *h₃mbʰ-* ​(proto-indo-european, "navel"). ‌Greek ὀμφαλός ​'navel, boss, ​centre'; the ​Delphic omphalos ​marked the ​world's centre ‌in archaic Greek ​geography.

The ‌ASCII form ​*omphalos* survives ‌only because ​the early ‌domain-name system ​could not ‌carry diacritics; ​it is ​a technological ‌compromise, not an ‌ancient spelling. ‌The Unicode ​restoration **Omphalós** ​recovers the ‌stress accent ​of the ​original directly ‌in the ​address bar. ​The original ‌preserves one prosodic ​feature — ‌stress or ​vowel length ​— rather ​than both, ​which places ‌the name ‌in Tier ​2.

The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

- **o** ​→ **O** ‌— Omicron
‌- **m** ‌→ **m** ‌— Mu
​- **p** ‌→ **p** ​— Pi
​- **h** ​→ **h** ‌— Eta aspiration ​(rough breathing ​marker in ​source)
- ‌**a** → ​**a** — ​Alpha
- ​**l** → ‌**l** — ​Lambda
- ‌**o** → ​**ó** — Acute ‌on omicron
​- **s** ‌→ **s** ‌— Sigma

​The project ​holds the ​domain **omphalós.com** ​(xn--omphals-q0a.com) as ‌the canonical ‌home of ​this name[^2].

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/omphalos/** ​— ​Greek ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**O** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Omphalós.
‌- ​**mphalós** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Greek tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'OMPHALOS' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Greek** ​— Omphalós, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Omphalós ​is Tier ‌2 ​because ‌the ​Greek ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Omphalós** circulate ‌within ​the Greek ​corpus, ​where the ​figure embodies ​navel, ‌center, delphi.[^1]

​### ​Primary Attestation ‌(Sources)

Omphalós ​is ‌attested in ​the canonical ‌Greek ​sources as ​a ​figure associated ​with navel, ​center, ‌delphi.[^2]

### ​Name ‌and Meaning ​(Etymology)

The ‌name ​means "Navel ‌(of ​the earth); ‌the stone ​at ​Delphi regarded ‌as the ‌centre ‌of the ​world" ​and reflects ‌the figure's ​role ​in the ‌tradition. ​The **Omphalos** ​stone at ‌Delphi ​was revered ‌as the ​navel ​of the ​inhabited ​world. According ‌to Hesiodic ‌and ​Delphic tradition, ‌Zeus ​released two ​eagles from ‌opposite ‌ends of ‌the earth; ‌they ​met at ‌Delphi, ​and the ​spot was ​marked ‌by the ​stone.[^1] ​The Pythia, ​Apollo's oracular ‌priestess, ​sat beside ​it ​when she ‌spoke. The ​stone ‌thus binds ​together cosmography, ‌kingship, ​and prophetic ‌speech: ‌to stand ​at the ​omphalos ​was to ​stand ‌at the ‌axis of ​order.
